questions.question:
With reference to the Chola inscriptions, consider the following statements:
A. The Uttaramur inscription provides details about the organisation of the sabha in Chola local administration.
B. It belongs to the reign of the Chola king Parantaka I and is dated to 919 CE and 921 CE.
C. It provides evidence of the Chola empire's military conquests in Sri Lanka.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
A and B only
The Uttaramur inscription (919 CE, 921 CE) issued during the reign of Parantaka I gives detailed information on the functioning of village assemblies (sabhas), rules of election, qualifications and disqualifications of members, and reflects India's long tradition of self-governance. It does not provide evidence of military conquests in Sri Lanka.

questions.question: In the 11th century, the army of which of the following Cholas reached upto Ganga to invade Bengal?
questions.solution:
Rajendra I (1014-1044 CE)
He was also known as Gangaikonda Chola. He defeated Mahipala, the Pala king of Bengal and Bihar.

questions.question: Who among the following rulers invaded Malaya to liberate their trade with China?
questions.solution: Chola dynasty

questions.question: Sabha and Ur, two kinds of village assemblies are referred to in which of the following dynasties?
questions.solution:
Chola
  • Ur - Assembly of common villagers
  • Sabha - Assembly in the villages which were inhabited by Brahmins

questions.question: The term 'Vellanvagai' in Chola inscriptions meant:
questions.solution:
Land gifted to Brahman
There were five types of land gifts that Chola kings gave to their people based on Chola inscriptions:
  • Vellanvagai - For non-Brahmana, peasant proprietors
  • Shalabhoga - For the maintenance of a school
  • Devadana or Tirunamattukkani - Land gifted to temples
  • Pallichchhandam - Land donated to Jaina institutions
  • Brahmadeya - Land gifted to Brahmins

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Airavatesvara Temple:
1. The Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram was built by Rajaraja Chola II.
2. The temple is dedicated to Lord Vishnu and is part of the Vaishnava temple group.
3. Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II renovated the temple in the 18th century.
Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect?
questions.solution:
2 and 3
The Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram (Tamil Nadu) was built by Rajaraja Chola II in the 12th century and is dedicated to Lord Shiva. Hence, Statements 2 and 3 are incorrect.

questions.question: The term 'Vetti' in Chola empire is related to
questions.solution:
Forced labour
Some types of taxes in Chola empire:
  • Kadmai or Irai - Tax on land
  • Pattam and ayam - Taxes imposed on non-agricultural professions like artisans and merchants
  • Nirvilia or nirkkirai - Water tax
  • Ulku and sungam - Toll tax
  • Tattar-pattam - A tax levied on gold-smiths
  • Sangam - Export and import taxes
  • Kannala Kanam - Marriage tax
  • Poorvi - War tax
  • Vetti - Forced labour

questions.question: Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni was a contemporary of which Chola king?
questions.solution: Rajendra I who ruled from 1014 to 1044 CE. Ghazni invaded India seventeen times. In 1018 he plundered the holy city of Mathura and also attacked Kannauj.

questions.question: In the early eleventh century, the Chola king Rajendra I built a Shiva temple and filled it with a Sun-pedestal seized from the
questions.solution:
Chalukyas
Chola king Rajendra I (reigned between 1014 and 1044 CE) built a Shiva temple in his capital, Gangaikondacholapuram (north Tamil Nadu) and filled it with prized statues seized from defeated rulers: Sun-pedestal (Chalukyas), a Ganesha statue and several statues of Durga, a Nandi statue, an image of Bhairava and Bhairavi (Kalingas of Orissa), and a Kali statue (Palas of Bengal).

questions.question: Who among the following belonged to the ancient chiefly family of the Cholas from Uraiyur, captured the Kaveri delta from the Muttaraiyar in the middle of the ninth century?
questions.solution:
Vijayalaya
He founded the Chola Empire and captured Thanjavur (Capital of Chola Empire) in 850 CE. He constructed a temple for the goddess Nishumbhasudini in Thanjavur.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding temple towns in medieval India:
1. Bhillasvamin developed as a temple town during the Chola dynasty.
2. Ajmer was the chief temple town patronised by the Cholas.
3. Ahmednagar grew as an important temple town under the Cholas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
1 only
Bhillasvamin was the temple town that flourished under the Chola dynasty. Ajmer and Ahmednagar were not Chola temple towns; they developed under other dynasties.

questions.question: Which of the following territories to the south and north were made part of the Chola kingdom by the successors of the ruler Vijayalaya?
questions.solution:
Pandyan and Pallava
  • Pallava dynasty (275 CE to 897 CE, Capital - Kanchipuram) ruled in Deccan (Tondaimandalam)
  • Pandya (Capital - Madurai)
  • Cheras (Capital - Vanji), Greatest ruler of Cheras - Senguttuvan, also known as Red Chera

questions.question: Which dynasty's bronze statues were made using the 'lost wax technique'?
questions.solution:
Chola
Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin. The lost wax technique is a method of metal casting in which molten metal is poured into a mold that has been created by means of a wax model. Examples: Nataraja Bronze Casting, Shiva and Parvati (Sivagami, 1012 CE), etc.

questions.question: Puhar or Kaveripattinam, was the port of which of the following dynasty?
questions.solution:
Cholas (8th-12th century AD)
It was founded by Vijayalaya in the 8th century. Rajaraja Chola (greatest king of the Chola Empire) reigned between 985 and 1014 CE.

questions.question: Which Pala ruler is known for founding the great Buddhist university at Vikramashila?
questions.solution:
Dharmapala (770-810 CE)
The second ruler of the Pala Dynasty and son of Gopala, he greatly expanded the empire's power in northern and eastern India. His reign was notable for the tripartite struggle over Kanauj against the Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas. A devoted Buddhist, he founded the famous Vikramashila monastery in Bihar and also revived Nalanda University. Under his patronage, art, architecture, and scholarship flourished. Dharmapala is remembered as the most powerful and influential Pala ruler.

questions.question: Whom Hiuen Tsang called 'one of the four lights of world', who's also called Indian Einstein?
questions.solution:
Nagarjuna
He was a 2nd-century Indian philosopher who founded the Madhyamaka school of Mahayana Buddhism. Hiuen Tsang praised him as "one of the four lights of the world" for his intellectual depth. Due to his profound philosophical insights, he is also known as the "Indian Einstein."

questions.question: Which dynasty was founded by Dantidurga in the mid-8th century?
questions.solution:
Rashtrakuta Dynasty
Dantidurga (c. 735-756 CE) is credited with founding the Rashtrakuta Dynasty in the Deccan region. He overthrew the Chalukyas of Badami and established Rashtrakuta power with his capital at Manyakheta (present-day Malkhed in Karnataka). The dynasty later rose to prominence under rulers like Govinda III and Amoghavarsha I, becoming one of the most powerful empires of early medieval India. The Rashtrakutas were great patrons of art, architecture, and literature (e.g., the famous Kailasa Temple at Ellora was built under King Krishna I).
  • Chola Dynasty - Ancient Tamil dynasty, revived later by Vijayalaya Chola (9th century)
  • Pala Dynasty - Founded by Gopala in Bengal (8th century)
  • Pratihara Dynasty - Founded by Nagabhata I in Rajasthan (8th century)

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Great Stupa of Amaravati:
1. The walls of the Great Stupa of Amaravati in the Lower Godavari region were adorned with bas relief sculptures.
2. The Amaravati school of art flourished under the patronage of the Mauryan rulers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
1 only
The Amaravati school of art flourished under the patronage of the Satavahanas in the Andhra region. Nagarjunkonda, another notable site, is renowned for its Buddhist architecture.

questions.question:
Select the correct alternative on the given statements based on Ashoka's Lion capital and India's State Emblem.
Statement I: In the original Ashoka's Lion Capital, there are four lions mounted back-to-back on a circular abacus that itself rests on a bell-shaped lotus.
Statement II: The State Emblem is an adaptation of the Lion Capital of Asoka at Sarnath in which the bell-shaped lotus was omitted.
questions.option_2: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
questions.option_3: Neither Statement I nor Statement II is true.
questions.solution:
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
The Lion Capital of Ashoka, carved around 250 BCE, is the head of a column erected by Emperor Ashoka at Sarnath, near Varanasi, India. Ashoka, the 3rd ruler of the Mauryan Empire (c. 268-232 BCE), governed a vast territory that stretched from present-day Afghanistan to Bangladesh, with Pataliputra as its capital.

questions.question: Sun temple at Modhera was built by which of the following rulers?
questions.solution:
Raja Bhimdev I
He was a Chaulukya king who ruled parts of present-day Gujarat, India. The Sun Temple of Modhera, dedicated to the solar deity Surya, is located in Modhera village, Mehsana district, Gujarat, on the bank of the river Pushpavati.

questions.question: Kautilya has mentioned the concept of Saptanga Rajya to understand the State with seven organs and one of them is Danda, which means:
questions.solution:
Force
Kautilya, also known as Chanakya, outlined the Saptanga theory of the state in the Arthashastra, identifying seven key components:
  • Swami (King)
  • Amatya (Minister)
  • Janapada (Territory)
  • Durga (Fort)
  • Kosa (Treasure)
  • Danda (Army or Force)
  • Mitra (Ally)

questions.question: The Dhakeshwari Temple in present day Bangladesh has been constructed under the rule of which dynasty?
questions.solution:
Sena
The National Temple of Bangladesh is the Dhakeshwari Temple, located in the capital, Dhaka. Dhakeshwari means "Goddess of Dhaka" and was built in the 12th century by King Ballal Sen of the Sena dynasty.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the construction of Nalanda University:
1. The excavated ruins of Nalanda University indicate that bright red bricks were used in its construction.
2. Nalanda University was founded by Ashoka the Great.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
1 only
The Ancient Nalanda University was founded by Kumaragupta I. Nalanda University was destroyed in 1193 CE by Bakhtiyar Khilji, a Turkish military general. The Chinese scholars I-Qing and Xuan Zang visited Nalanda in the 7th century CE. The ancient Nalanda was a centre of learning from the 5th century CE to 12th century CE. Located in present-day Rajgir, Bihar.

questions.question: Who excavated the Chira Tope stupa at Taxila?
questions.solution:
John Marshall
Dharmarajika Stupa in Taxila, Pakistan is also known as Chir Tope, which means "Scarred hill".

questions.question: Which among the following dynasties originated from the Yueh-chih tribe of China?
questions.solution:
Kushanas
They migrated from China to Bactria, then to areas of Afghanistan and finally into India around the 1st century CE.

questions.question: Details about Sudarshana lake are given in a rock inscription at Girnar (Junagarh), which was composed to record the achievements of the Shaka ruler
questions.solution:
Rudradaman I
Junagadh inscription is written in the Sanskrit language. It is located near Girnar hill near Junagadh in Gujarat. The Junagadh rock contains inscriptions of Ashoka (one of the fourteen Major Rock Edicts of Ashoka), Rudradaman I and Skandagupta.

questions.question: Silappathikaram (the Jewelled Anklet), the earliest epic poem in Tamil was written in the 5th-6th Century CE by
questions.solution:
Ilango Adigal
Ancient Tamil literature is known as Sangama Literature. The Sangam literature includes Tolkappiyam, Ettutogai, Pattuppattu, Pathinenkilkanakku, and two epics named - Silappathikaram, and Manimegalai (Written by Sittalai Sattanar). The earliest known work in ancient Tamil is Agastyam.

questions.question: In the 7th Century AD, a new religion called Islam was born in
questions.solution:
Arabia
Prophet Muhammad established Islam. He was born around 570 AD in Mecca. In 622 AD, he completed the Hegira, his migration from Mecca to Medina, to escape persecution.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Gautamiputra Satakarni:
1. Gautamiputra Satakarni, titled Rajaraja and Maharaja, belonged to the Shunga dynasty.
2. The Satavahana dynasty, founded by Simuka, primarily ruled over present-day Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Telangana, and parts of Gujarat, Karnataka, and Madhya Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
2 only
The Satavahana Dynasty, founded by Simuka, primarily encompassed present-day Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Telangana, along with portions of Gujarat, Karnataka, and Madhya Pradesh. Gautamiputra Satakarni belonged to the Satavahana dynasty, not the Shunga dynasty.

questions.question: Valabhi, a city of ancient India was the capital of the ______ dynasty from the 5th to 8th Century CE.
questions.solution:
Maitraka
The Maitraka dynasty was founded by Senapati Bhatarka. The decline of the Gupta Empire led to the rise of various ruling dynasties across northern India. Among the most notable were the Pushyabhutis of Thanesar, the Maukharis of Kanauj, and the Maitrakas of Valabhi.
